claim: coalition {2, 3, 4}: no strictly positive z solves M z = 0, where M is the principal submatrix of the unilateral matrix on players 2, 3, 4 -- its (i,j) entry is the shifted payoff to the i-th of them when the j-th quits alone, so the system says every member of the coalition is indifferent while all of them quit at a positive rate. The conditions below are the linear forms (M^T y)_i with the payoff entries as their coefficients, and the point is the y that makes them non-negative and not all zero: any z > 0 with M z = 0 would then give 0 = <M z, y> = <z, M^T y> > 0. This is the hypothesis of (L8) for this coalition (docs/G3_MIXED_APS.md 12.2).
